CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Summary

There is no branch listing/switching API today, and — importantly — **branch switching was tried and deliberately removed** from the app for reasons documented in the code. I found a clear architectural directive that a "branch switcher" should probably not switch a workroom's branch in place, but instead create a new workroom for the target branch. Details below, with file:line references.

### 1. LIST all local branches/bookmarks — does not exist as a public API

- `VCSProviding` (`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16-53`) has no `listBranches`/`listBookmarks` method. It only exposes `log`, `changeset`, `fileDiff`, `workingFileDiff`, `fileContent`, `commitParentFileContent`, `workingBaseFileContent`, `currentRef`.
- **jj side**, the closest existing thing is a *private* helper inside `CLIVCSWriter` (the write-side CLI shim), used only to compute ahead/behind counts for the toolbar, not exposed for a picker:
  - `CLIVCSWriter.jjBookmarkListArgs()` — `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift:712-727` — builds `jj bookmark list --all-remotes` args with a template emitting name/remote/target/present/conflict/tracked/ahead/behind.
  - `CLIVCSWriter.parseJJBookmarks(_:primaryRemote:)` — `VCSWriting.swift:1027-1066` — parses that into `[JJBookmark]` (`struct JJBookmark { let name: String; let tracking: VCSTracking? }`, `VCSWriting.swift:1009-1012`).
  - Called only from `private func jjRemoteState(...)` — `VCSWriting.swift:1474-1478` — i.e. it lists bookmarks purely to compute sync/tracking state for the current bookmark, not to enumerate options for switching.
  - In the Rust core, `bookmark_map(repo: &ReadonlyRepo)` (`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/src/jj_backend.rs:111-120`) builds `commit_id -> [bookmark names]` from `repo.view().local_bookmarks()`, but it's used only to decorate History rows (`current_ref`'s ancestor walk), and is **not exposed through UniFFI** — `wr-vcs-uniffi/src/lib.rs` only exports `probe_repo`, `log_page`, `changeset`, `current_ref`, `working_status` (all read-only; grep at `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/vcs/crates/wr-vcs-uniffi/src/lib.rs:309-350`).
- **git side**, `GitProvider.decorations(in:)` (`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitProvider.swift:379-391`) calls SwiftGitX's `repo.branch.list(.local)` to build `commit -> [branch names]` purely for History-row decoration — again not exposed as a "list branches" API.

So: bookmark/branch enumeration logic exists in two forms (jj CLI template + parser; git SwiftGitX `branch.list`), but both are private, single-purpose, and read-only-adjacent (used for decoration/tracking, not user-facing pickers).

### 2. SWITCH/CHECKOUT to a different branch — does not exist, and was explicitly removed

No `checkout`/`switch`/`edit`-onto-bookmark function exists anywhere in `VCSProviding` or `VCSWriting`. This is not an oversight — it's documented as an intentional removal:

- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/VCSToolbar.swift:200-207`:
  > "Segment 1: the current branch. **Display only — not a control.** Not a dropdown, and not a button either. Workrooms **are** branches — a workroom's identity is its directory name, with no branch field anywhere in the config — so switching a workroom's branch would make its name permanently wrong, and the jj equivalent (`jj new <bookmark>`) was reproduced removing a file from the working copy and orphaning the workroom's commit."
- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/TODOS.md:929-959` (`### "New workroom from branch…" (macapp) — the successor to branch switching`):
  - git: `internal/vcs/git.go` creates a workroom via `git worktree add -b`; there's no `branch` field in `internal/config`, so re-pointing a workroom's branch leaves its directory name permanently wrong with nothing to reconcile.
  - jj: `jj new <bookmark>` on the bookmark the toolbar displays was **measured** to remove a file from the working copy and leave the workroom's commit as a nameless dangling head, with no visible change in the UI.
  - The recommended successor feature is explicitly **"Pick a local or remote branch and create a workroom for it"** — not switching in place. Suggested starting points: `Views/OpenWorkroomDialog.swift` (searchable, project-grouped picker to model the UI on), the Go CLI's `create` (already accepts a branch), and `CLIVCSWriter.gitRemoteRefsArgs` (`VCSWriting.swift:426-430`) for cheaply enumerating remote refs.

**This is the single most important finding for your feature** — if your "branch switcher" means switching an existing workroom's checked-out branch in place, the codebase has already tried that twice (git and jj) and pulled it back out for correctness reasons. The documented, sanctioned direction is "new workroom from branch," which sidesteps the identity/dangling-head problems.

### 3. Closest existing patterns to model a new implementation on

If you still need something switch-like (or the "new workroom from branch" successor), the best models are:

- **Current-ref lookup** (read-only precedent for both backends):
  - `VCSProviding.currentRef(root:)` — `VCSProviding.swift:52` — `func currentRef(root: URL) async throws -> VCSRef`.
  - `GitProvider.currentRef` — `GitProvider.swift:78-99` (via SwiftGitX `repo.branch.current`).
  - `RustJJProvider.currentRef` — `RustJJProvider.swift:48-59` (via `WrVcs.currentRef`, itself `jj_backend::current_ref` at `vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/src/jj_backend.rs:416-441`).
  - `BranchResolver.resolve(path:vcs:)` — `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/BranchResolver.swift:30-45` — the per-call-timeout wrapper pattern used to surface it in the sidebar; a branch-switcher UI's "what's currently checked out" read should follow this same shape (timeout-wrapped, best-effort, never blocks other rows).

- **CLI shell-out write pattern** (this is the pattern any new mutating branch op should follow — `VCSWriting`/`CLIVCSWriter`, not `VCSProviding`):
  - `VCSWriting` protocol — `VCSWriting.swift:227-260` — the seam for writes (fetch/push/pull/commit), explicitly separated from `VCSProviding` because writes must go through the snapshot/lock gate.
  - `CLIVCSWriter` — `VCSWriting.swift:318-344` — shells real `git`/`jj` binaries (not SwiftGitX, not jj-lib) for every write, with a documented rationale (`VCSWriting.swift:289-293`): SwiftGitX 0.4.0 has no credential path for fetch/push and no pull at all; jj-lib has no Swift API for writes at all.
  - Argument-builder pattern to copy: `jjRebaseArgs(onto:)` (`VCSWriting.swift:869-871`, using `jjWriteFlags` not `jjReadFlags`), `jjCommitArgs(message:)` (`VCSWriting.swift:887-889`), `gitPullArgs`/`gitPushArgs` (`VCSWriting.swift:522-525`, `491-495`) — each is a **pure static arg-builder**, unit-tested without spawning a process, then invoked via `run(...)`/`runNetwork` inside an instance method gated by `JJSnapshotGate`.   - Placement logic to reuse: `CLIVCSWriter.opDirectory(_:path:projectRoot:)` (`VCSWriting.swift:368-373`) — a branch-switch write, like push/pull/commit, must run in the **workroom** directory, not the project root, for the same reason documented there (a jj write at the root can operate on the ROOT workspace's `@`, not the workroom's).

### 4. git (SwiftGitX) vs jj (jj-lib UniFFI vs CLI) structure, and write-op gotchas

**Structure**, per `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/CLAUDE.md` ("VCS core" section) and the code itself:
- **git**: `GitProvider` (`GitProvider.swift`) is pure Swift over SwiftGitX (libgit2), used for ALL reads (`log`, `changeset`, `currentRef`, `fileDiff`, `workingStatus`, etc.) — no subprocess. Three narrow reads reach past SwiftGitX directly into raw libgit2 C API (`GitGraph`, `GitCommitDiff`, `GitDiffStats`) for capabilities SwiftGitX lacks (commit-range revwalk, rename detection, diffstat) — see `macapp/CLAUDE.md`'s "VCS core" section for the full rationale.
- **jj**: reads (`log`, `changeset`, `currentRef`, `workingStatus`) go through `RustJJProvider` → `WrVcs.*` (UniFFI) → `wr-vcs-core::jj_backend` (native jj-lib, no subprocess) — see `macapp/CLAUDE.md`: *"the jj CLI parsers are gone — log/changeset/currentRef/workingStatus are all native jj-lib."* But `RustJJProvider.fileDiff`/`workingFileDiff`/`fileContent` (`RustJJProvider.swift:97-217`) still shell out to the real `jj` CLI, because jj-lib exposes no git-format diff writer and no ergonomic file-content read — "the plan's sanctioned CLI fallback for ops jj-lib doesn't expose ergonomically" (`RustJJProvider.swift:130-133`).
- **All writes, both backends**, go through `CLIVCSWriter` shelling the real `git`/`jj` binaries (`VCSWriting.swift:318-344`) — there is **no jj-lib write path at all** in this codebase currently, and no SwiftGitX write path either (both explicitly ruled out per the doc at `VCSWriting.swift:289-293`).

- **jj-lib's one existing mutating READ already documents the exact hazard a switch would hit.** `macapp/CLAUDE.md`: *"The one mutating read: `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`. jj's working copy is itself a commit, so on-disk edits don't exist to jj-lib until snapshotted — a working-copy status read therefore must snapshot `@` first: it takes the working-copy lock and rewrites `@`."* A branch switch (`jj new <bookmark>`/`jj edit <bookmark>`) is a much bigger mutation of the same kind — it rewrites `@` and moves the working-copy pointer — so it needs the same lock discipline, but as a full write, not a read-triggered side-effect.
